subject: Post-demo: token unit-econ proposal & purchase path
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Morris <janelle@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + draft unit-econ scenarios (attached)

Thanks again for the demo time earlier today — great conversation. Taking the notes from our call and the numbers you shared, I wanted to send a concise recap, an initial unit-econ estimate, and proposed next steps so procurement and engineering have a clear path forward. I attached a working spreadsheet and the raw rate table for transparency.

Call notes (quick):
- Primary use: clinical triage & patient messaging (NLG + retrieval).
- Peak daily queries you mentioned: ~700k; expected average: ~400k.
- Avg tokens per request (current sample): ~450 tokens.
- Customer requirement: HIPAA posture + SOC 2 Type II evidence; latency SLOs around 300–500ms for single-turn responses.

Redwood rough model (attached: catalyst_pricing_model_v3.xlsx / redwood_token_rate_table.csv):
- Baseline monthly volume we modeled: 180M tokens/month (400k calls * 450 tokens avg).
- Budget range you shared on call: $15k–$25k / month (marketing/ops estimate).
- You mentioned target unit cost goal: ~ $90–$120 per 1M tokens as a negotiation target.

Three quick scenarios in the sheet (summary):
1) Pilot (3–4 weeks): 0–50M tokens, hosted plan, no commit — list price in sheet (est. $7k total)
2) Production (monthly avg 180M tokens): flat per-1M at $95 yields ~$17,100 + $1,500 platform fee = ~$18.6k/mo
3) Committed (12-mo reserved capacity): blended $85/1M for 180M = ~$15.3k/mo + reserved capacity fee (detailed in sheet)

Notes and levers we included: KV/prefix caching savings (we modeled ~12% token reduction for repeated prompts), suggested autoscale buffer for peak days, and optional dedicated pool line item (for guaranteed latency/SLA). The spreadsheet includes an alternate breakdown showing a tiered block price if you prefer step-pricing instead of flat unit.

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm average monthly token expectation (is 180M closer to your planning mean or is peak your budgeting anchor)?
- If 180M looks reasonable, would Catalyst consider a 12-month commit for the discounted blended rate?
- Please loop in procurement contact for PO timing — if we agree on economics we can push MSA + SOW to DocuSign.
- We’ll start a security package: SOC 2 artifact handoff and the basic questionnaire once we have the procurement POC contact.

Attachments (stubs):
- catalyst_pricing_model_v3.xlsx (calculator + scenario tabs)
- redwood_token_rate_table.csv (per-model per-1M rates used in calc)
- estimate_summary.pdf (one-pager with the 3 scenarios)

If useful I can also produce a single-line invoice mock that shows the math for the month you want to budget against. Happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up later this week.

Best,
Soojin Lee | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — this is super helpful. A couple clarifications from our side so your models match internal expectations:
- The 700k was a peak for a very specific pilot segment (appointments routing). The production average we expect across all cohorts is nearer to ~400k requests/day on peak weeks, which maps to ~120–200M tokens/month depending on seasonality.
- We can commit to a 3‑month production pilot (not just a short dev pilot) with monitored success metrics; procurement is comfortable approving that scope quickly.
- Budget: our internal stretch target sits around $95/1M tokens for production (we can go up to $120 for a year-commit if latency and SLA are strong).

Request: can you send a single-line example invoice for 180M tokens at $95/1M (plus any platform fee) so procurement can model cashflow? Also call out what guarantees we get at the $95 vs $85 committed tier (latency/throughput differences).

We’re keen to move fast if security and legal timelines look reasonable. Looping procurement and Evan (engineering lead) to confirm the 3-month pilot scope and success criteria.

— Janelle

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + draft unit-econ scenarios (attached) — updated estimate & recommended offer

Soojin / Vivek —
Following Janelle's note, I updated the pricing scenarios and produced a concise one-line invoice example and a recommended commercial path. Files attached (I updated the filename in the thread): catalyst_pricing_model_v4.xlsx and estimate_summary.pdf.

Highlights / recommendation (quick):
- Pilot (3-month production pilot): capped to 50M tokens/month for a predictable spend window. Pilot rate: $150/1M for the first 50M (credit applied for onboarding) + $2k platform fee / month.
- Production (no commit, expected 120–200M): offer a flat $95/1M + $1,500 platform fee. This directly answers procurement's modeling ask (we'll attach the one-line invoice example).
- Committed (12-month reserve): blended $85/1M with a committed capacity credit and SLA add-ons (guaranteed reserved pool with 99.9% uptime SLO).

Example invoice math (one-line model we put in estimate_summary.pdf):
- Scenario: 180M tokens @ $95/1M = 180 * $95 = $17,100
- Platform fee = $1,500
- Total = $18,600 / month (billing stub shows token line + platform fee)

Operational caveats:
- KV caching: estimated 10–15% effective token reduction for common patient prompts — we included a conservative 12% cache savings in the workbook.
- Latency: Hosted shared pools typically land in 300–600ms for this workload; dedicated pool is where we consistently hit under 300ms at scale. Details in the SLA addendum (we will have legal attach).

Action items I can take on:
- Prep a one-line invoice PDF and a short pilot SOW to define success metrics (engagement rate, latency, fallback rates).
- Start security artifact handoff (SOC 2 evidence) once procurement provides the data room contact.
- If we want committed pricing, I can draft reserved-capacity terms for 12 months and show the delta to the $95 flat model.

Attaching: catalyst_pricing_model_v4.xlsx, estimate_summary.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick alignment call with procurement and Evan if you want me there.

Aisha Rahman | Senior GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
